{{nihongo|'''Kandani Shrine'''|神谷神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Sanuki Province]].

'''Kandani Shrine''' (かんだにじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Sakaide, Kagawa|Q855059|qid=Q855059}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|Q161454|qid=Q161454}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}} it was a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Overview ===
It stands on the slope of Shiramine-yama, one of the peaks of {{ill|Goshikidai|Q11372616|qid=Q11372616}}, in the eastern part of Sakaide. It is located in a valley called "Kandani," with the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kandani River}} flowing north of the precinct.

Its honden is the oldest known {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} shrine building with a clearly known construction year<ref>[http://www.shikoku.gr.jp/spot/380 Kandani Shrine]</ref>, and is designated a National Treasure. Although it possesses a National Treasure shrine building, the precinct itself is relatively small. It also preserves shrine treasures including nationally designated Important Cultural Property standing attendant statues.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
According to shrine tradition, the valley where the shrine stands has long been called "Kandani." Behind the shrine is a giant rock called "Eikō-seki," identified as an ancient {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}} sacred rock, and Yayoi pottery has been found nearby.

Regarding its founding, tradition states that in {{ill|812|Q31114|qid=Q31114}} ({{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} 3), Atto Ōtaru, uncle of {{ill|Kūkai|Q222227|qid=Q222227}}, built shrine buildings and invited the Kasuga Four Deities into the co-enshrined hall.

In {{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 7), it was granted Junior Fifth Rank Upper; in {{ill|868|Q25061|qid=Q25061}} (Jogan 10), Senior Fifth Rank Lower. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Shrines}} compiled in {{ill|905|Q24239|qid=Q24239}} ({{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} 5), it appears in {{ill|Sanuki Province|Q929682|qid=Q929682}}{{ill|Aya district|Q11658001|qid=Q11658001}} as "Kandani Shrine," listed as a Shikinaisha. The ridge beam of the current honden bears an ink inscription from {{ill|1219|Q5388|qid=Q5388}} ({{ill|Kempo (era)|Q1194251|qid=Q1194251}} 7): "Treasure hall of Senior First Rank Kandani Daimyojin... begun on 10th day, 2nd month, year of tsuchinoto-u... by manor official Gyōbu no Sukune Masanaga," showing it had reached the highest divine rank and regional reverence at that time.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} era, it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} under the modern shrine ranking system. On New Year's Eve of {{ill|1927|Q18110|qid=Q18110}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 2), a lamp fire ignited the haiden, causing a fire. The haiden burned down, but residents pulled the collapsing building away from the honden side, saving it. The present haiden was rebuilt from {{ill|1928|Q19715|qid=Q19715}} (Showa 3) to {{ill|1930|Q18787|qid=Q18787}} (Showa 5).

On {{ill|September 27|Q2884|qid=Q2884}}, {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} (Reiwa 4), lightning struck the honden and about one-third of the roof was burned<ref name="shikoku-np20220927">{{Cite web|和書|title=Kagawa: roof of National Treasure honden burned / lightning strike at Kandani Shrine |url=https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/national/social/20220927000464 |date=2022-09-27 |publisher=Shikoku Shimbun |accessdate=2022-09-27}}</ref>. On October 12, {{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} (Reiwa 5), a ground-breaking ceremony for preservation and repair was held, with completion planned for autumn 2025<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=First step toward restoration of National Treasure honden: ground-breaking at Kandani Shrine in Sakaide, roof repair planned to finish autumn 2025 |url=https://www.shikoku-np.co.jp/dg/article.aspx?id=K2023101300000001400 |date=2023-10-13 |publisher=Shikoku Shimbun |accessdate=2023-10-15}}</ref>.

=== Divine ranks ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 7 ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}), October 9: from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - recorded as "Kandani deity".
* Jogan 17 ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}), May 27: Senior Fifth Rank Lower (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') - recorded as "Kandani Tenjin".

=== Precinct ===
The honden is a three-bay nagare-zukuri shrine building rebuilt in {{ill|1219|Q5388|qid=Q5388}} (Kenpo 7), early {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, by manor official Gyōbu Masanaga from the old honden. It is the oldest known shrine architecture in Japan with a clear construction date and is designated a National Treasure.

About 50 meters behind the shrine buildings stands a giant rock called "Eikō-seki." It is said that in ancient times worship was performed there as an {{ill|Iwakura rock|Q11587880|qid=Q11587880}} sacred site.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== National Treasure ===
* Honden - designated {{ill|February 2|Q2313|qid=Q2313}}, {{ill|1955|Q18577|qid=Q18577}} (Showa 30).

=== Important Cultural Property (national designation) ===
* Two wooden standing attendant statues
*: A pair of A and Un figures, considered early Kamakura works. Designated {{ill|June 11|Q2617|qid=Q2617}}, {{ill|1966|Q2649|qid=Q2649}} (Showa 41).

=== Sakaide City designated tangible cultural properties ===
* Jinja Hōraku Renga (calligraphy)
*: A 100-verse {{ill|Renga|Q1506883|qid=Q1506883}} sequence performed before the shrine in {{ill|1493|Q6687|qid=Q6687}} ({{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 2), written on four half-folded torinoko sheets. Designated Feb 21, 1958.
* Two bugaku masks (craftworks)
*: Two masks for Batō and Kangenraku. Designated Nov 3, 1961.
* Hand-copied Daihannya Haramita Sutra, 600 volumes (documents)
*: Inscribed {{ill|1455|Q6480|qid=Q6480}} ({{ill|Kyōtoku|Q1143370|qid=Q1143370}} 4) and {{ill|1481|Q6631|qid=Q6631}} ({{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 13). Designated Jan 10, 1967.
